visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 at least presents the correct problem statement and a relevant nested-circle diagram, whereas Lesson 1 shows a blank title screen and a garbled, positionally unhelpful formula/text that does not accurately visualize the shaded-ring setup.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 includes a well-formed, wired quiz gate after act_summation with a real question, plausible options, and a correct answer, whereas Lesson 1 has no available gate specs or plan and therefore no functioning interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 provides clear, mostly natural spoken narration with no raw LaTeX or garbled text, while Lesson 1 has no available narration transcript and therefore cannot demonstrate any audio clarity or pacing quality.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 provides timed visual cues that mostly coincide with the narrated references to drawing, shading, formulas, graphing, and final answer, whereas Lesson 1 has no transcript or cue data at all, making its visual-narration sync absent and unevaluable.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 correctly and clearly derives each shaded ring area, sums to πn(2n+1), and solves the minimum inequality, while Lesson 1 has no available transcript or lesson content to verify any accurate explanation.

polish.rationale: Lesson 1 is far more visually polished with a large centered formula and legible styling, whereas Lesson 2 has raw unrendered LaTeX, visible player controls, tiny/off-corner diagrams and labels, empty boxes, and excessive unused space.

aggregator.explanation: Lesson 2 is the clear overall winner: five of six agents favored it with high confidence across visual accuracy, interactivity, narration quality, synchronization, and conceptual accuracy. It presents the correct problem, relevant visuals, functioning quiz interaction, clear narration, mostly aligned timing cues, and an accurate mathematical derivation. Lesson 1 only won polish, with the agent noting stronger visual styling, but this is outweighed by Lesson 2's much stronger instructional correctness, completeness, narration, sync, and interactivity.
